Rajni pulled a crumpled paper from her son's bag and smoothed it on the kitchen table.
“Twenty-one out of fifty?”
“Give it back.” Eshaan didn't look up. “Don't tell Papa. I'll fix it.”
“You used to draw until midnight. Now you say nothing at all. Eshaan, do you even like physics?”
“It doesn't matter. Papa and Bhaiya are engineers. That's the plan.”
“Who asked you if you wanted it?”
“Nobody had to.” He rubbed the edge of the table. “I sit in class and my head is somewhere else. I hid the last two tests as well.”
Rajni sat down slowly. “Two tests. And I only noticed today.”
He finally glanced up. “Are you angry?”
“No. I'm wondering why none of us asked.”

When I was choosing streams in Class 10, there was no discussion. My father is an engineer. My elder brother is an engineer. Everyone assumed the younger son would be one too. So I took science, maths and physics, and I never once asked whether I liked any of it.

I'm Chaitanya, and by Class 11 I was bored in almost every class. The only thing I looked forward to was the Friday history club, where Gautam and I argued about the Mughals.

My physics marks dropped to 38. Then 31. I hid the report card in my school bag and told my father the results "weren't out yet". Every evening at dinner, when he asked about JEE preparation, I said "fine" and looked at my plate.

Gautam asked me once, "Did you ever want this?" I didn't have an answer. I'd never asked myself.

qa.q: What did Chaitanya's physics marks drop to?
How did Chaitanya feel at dinner when asked about preparation?
qa.a: Chaitanya felt guilty and trapped, saying "fine" while looking at the plate.

qa.q: What should Chaitanya have done before choosing the stream?
qa.a: Asked honestly what subjects interested him and discussed it with his father, rather than following the family pattern without checking.

qa.q: How might Chaitanya's father see things if he learned the truth?
qa.a: He would probably feel hurt about being misled and worried, and might wish he had asked what Chaitanya wanted.

grounding: A reflective account of a student choosing science because the father and elder brother are engineers, never asking about liking it, and by Class 11 bored and hiding poor marks.

Class teacher's note, Class 11 Science, mid-year

Yogesh's marks have fallen in all three science subjects since April: physics from 62 to 35. He is polite, but in class he looks out of the window, and he has stopped submitting practical files.

On Tuesday his friend Raghav stayed back and told me, worried, that Yogesh had hidden his last two report cards from his parents. I spoke to Yogesh privately. He said he took science because his father and his older brother both work as engineers and "it was just decided". He said he has never liked it and did not think he was allowed to say so. He enjoys accounts and business studies, which he reads on his own.

I told him he was not in trouble with me. I called his parents that evening and have arranged a meeting with them and the school counsellor on Friday to talk about his interests and his options.

qa.q: What did Yogesh's physics marks fall to?
How might Yogesh have felt about his stream choice?
qa.a: He probably felt bored and trapped, believing he was not allowed to say he never liked science.

qa.q: What else could the teacher do at Friday's meeting?
qa.a: The teacher could invite Yogesh to explain what he enjoys, with the counsellor helping the family look at options like commerce.

qa.q: How might Raghav have felt staying back to tell the teacher?
qa.a: Raghav was probably worried and uneasy about betraying a friend, but cared enough to speak.

grounding: A teacher's note shows a student who took science because his father and elder brother are engineers, never asked if he liked it, and by Class 11 is bored and hiding marks.
